title: Meet Neutro: Your Flu Season Bouncer
description:
Flu season is coming for the 6ix, so who pulls up first? Neutro, your neutrophil bouncer. When flu hits your airways, neutrophils are the first immune cells on the scene. Cyto breaks it down, live from the 6ix.

Neutrophils have 3 big moves: they eat germs (phagocytosis), release toxic chemicals (degranulation and reactive oxygen species) and throw out sticky nets (NETs). But McMaster researchers call it a thin line between helpful and harmful: in severe flu, the same moves can hurt your lungs. Where that line sits still isn't well understood, and much of this research is in animals, whose neutrophils differ from ours. Your best defence is still the yearly flu shot.

Sources (via PubMed):
George et al. (McMaster), Vaccines 2021 (review): Neutrophils and Influenza: A Thin Line between Helpful and Harmful — https://doi.org/10.3390/vaccines9060597
Lamichhane & Samarasinghe, J Immunol Res 2019 (review) — https://doi.org/10.1155/2019/8028725

Ask a pharmacist or doctor about your flu shot. Not medical advice.
